column1: # Source: P. S. Modenov, Problems in Geometry, translated by George Yankovsky, Mir, Moscow, 1981
# (https://archive.org/details/ModenovProblemsInGeometryMir1981). Each row is a computation the book makes or rests on,
# cited in its source field by chapter, section and problem; the readings of #2131 found them, each checked by value.
# Fields, tab separated: id, source, op, var, input, expected, points, note.
#   zero     input is identically 0, and Simplify is to reduce it to 0
#   equal    input equals expected, and Simplify of the input is to reach a form no larger than expected
#   solve    input is an equation in var, and expected is the book's whole root set
#   erratum  the book prints expected where the value is input's; the library must not confirm the printed form
# points is where every free variable may be sampled: C complex, R real, P positive, U the unit circle, - none.
# The harness checks each row's own claim by value before asking the library, and fails on a row that does not hold.
# A conjugate is written as the book does on the unit circle, 1/z, or as a symbol of its own; a determinant as det.
# The note says what the reading saw the library do at 725481ca4; the verdict now is in modenov-baseline.tsv.
# Not here, because the harness cannot compare their values: a set by condition (Ch II §2 Exercise 4), a limit
# that is infinite (Ch IV §3 Problem 14), sums to a natural n and an infinite sum convergent only for |q| < 1
# (Ch V Appendix 4, 5, 6), and a congruence of angles (Ch V §2, p. 342).
